steps: To determine the ancestral state of a trait, one must use an outgroup comparison.
An outgroup is a taxon that is closely related to the group of interest but branched off earlier.
Option (B) suggests using a more distantly related snake, which serves as an appropriate outgroup.
Option (A) is ineffective because the fossil record is incomplete and lacks the necessary data.
Option (C) uses a mammal, which is too distantly related to provide meaningful evolutionary context for snake tongue morphology.
